    SELECT job_title_code
    FROM Staff_Department_Assignments
    GROUP BY job_title_code
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT department_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Departments)
)

    AVG(julianday(sda.date_assigned_to) - julianday(sda.date_assigned_from)) AS average_assignment_duration

WHERE sda.job_title_code IN (SELECT job_title_code FROM Job_Titles_In_All_Depts)

FROM Product_Suppliers ps

    FROM Order_Items oi
    JOIN Customer_Orders co ON oi.order_id = co.order_id
    JOIN Customers c ON co.customer_id = c.customer_id
    WHERE c.payment_method_code = 'Credit Card'
);

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I want the total value for each supplier separately, i.e., one total per supplier.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH credit_products AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT oi.product_id
    FROM Order_Items oi
    JOIN Customer_Orders co ON oi.order_id = co.order_id
    JOIN Customers c ON co.customer_id = c.customer_id
    WHERE c.payment_method_code = 'Credit Card'
)
SELECT ps.supplier_id,
       SUM(ps.total_value_purchased) AS total_value
FROM Product_Suppliers ps
JOIN credit_products cp ON ps.product_id = cp.product_id
GROUP BY ps.supplier_id
ORDER BY ps.supplier_id;

questions.nlq: Evaluate the progressive accumulation of procurement value attributable to all suppliers, presenting the data as a five-point trailing average of the daily totals.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: Clarification: I refer to the collection of all suppliers acting as a single entity; calculate the daily sum of values across the entire system, compute a global running total, and then apply the trailing average to that single sequence.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH daily_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE(date_supplied_from) AS purchase_date,
        SUM(total_value_purchased) AS daily_total
    FROM Product_Suppliers
    GROUP BY DATE(date_supplied_from)
)
SELECT 
    AVG(daily_total) OVER (
        ORDER BY purchase_date 
        ROWS BETWEEN 4 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS five_point_trailing_average
FROM daily_totals
ORDER BY purchase_date

meanings.hidden_knowledge: Clarification: I refer to the set of suppliers individually; calculate the daily sum of values for each specific supplier, compute a running total for each supplier separately, and then apply the trailing average to each supplier's individual sequence.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH daily_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        supplier_id,
        DATE(date_supplied_from) AS supply_date,
        SUM(total_value_purchased) AS daily_total
    FROM "Product_Suppliers"
    GROUP BY supplier_id, DATE(date_supplied_from)
),
running_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        supplier_id,
        supply_date,
        daily_total,
        SUM(daily_total) OVER (
            PARTITION BY supplier_id 
            ORDER BY supply_date
        ) AS running_total
    FROM daily_totals
)
SELECT 
    supplier_id,
    supply_date,
    AVG(running_total) OVER (
        PARTITION BY supplier_id 
        ORDER BY supply_date 
        ROWS BETWEEN 4 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS five_point_trailing_avg
FROM running_totals
ORDER BY supplier_id, supply_date;

FROM Products p
WHERE p.product_id IN (
    SELECT ps.product_id
    FROM Product_Suppliers ps
    GROUP BY ps.product_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ps.supplier_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Suppliers)
);

FROM Suppliers AS s
JOIN Product_Suppliers AS ps ON s.supplier_id = ps.supplier_id
JOIN Products AS p ON ps.product_id = p.product_id
ORDER BY s.supplier_name, p.product_name;

questions.nlq: Hey! Could you help me out? I'm trying to figure out which products were sold by all suppliers in 2017! I'd love to see their names and total purchase values.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I mean the products that EVERY single supplier had in their portfolio during 2017 - the ones they all offered in common. Only show me products that appeared in every supplier's records for that year.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT 
    p.product_name,
    SUM(ps.total_value_purchased) AS total_purchase_value
FROM Products p
INNER JOIN Product_Suppliers ps ON p.product_id = ps.product_id
WHERE ps.date_supplied_from <= '2017-12-31'
    AND (ps.date_supplied_to IS NULL OR ps.date_supplied_to >= '2017-01-01')
GROUP BY p.product_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ps.supplier_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Suppliers)

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I want to see which products EACH supplier offered during 2017 - list them out by supplier so I can see what each one provided separately.
meanings.gt_sql: SELECT p.product_name, ps.total_value_purchased, s.supplier_name FROM Products p JOIN Product_Suppliers ps ON p.product_id = ps.product_id JOIN Suppliers s ON ps.supplier_id = s.supplier_id WHERE (ps.date_supplied_from <= '2017-12-31' AND (ps.date_supplied_to IS NULL OR ps.date_supplied_to >= '2017-01-01'))

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I mean the combined total value purchased each year summed across all suppliers, so one number per year showing overall purchasing volume.
meanings.gt_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', date_supplied_from) AS year, SUM(total_value_purchased) AS total_value_purchased FROM Product_Suppliers GROUP BY year ORDER BY year;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I want the total value purchased per supplier for each year, listed separately for every supplier so I can see their individual contributions.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT s.supplier_name,
       strftime('%Y', ps.date_supplied_from) AS year,
       SUM(ps.total_value_purchased) AS total_value_purchased
FROM Product_Suppliers ps
JOIN Suppliers s ON ps.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
GROUP BY s.supplier_name, year
ORDER BY s.supplier_name, year;

SELECT p.product_name
FROM Products p
INNER JOIN Product_Suppliers ps ON p.product_id = ps.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ps.supplier_id) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT supplier_id) FROM Suppliers)

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I want to see each supplier's products separately, grouped by supplier.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT 
    s.supplier_name,
    p.product_name
FROM Suppliers s
JOIN Product_Suppliers ps ON s.supplier_id = ps.supplier_id
JOIN Products p ON ps.product_id = p.product_id
ORDER BY s.supplier_name, p.product_name

questions.nlq: Could you tell me the total purchase value for all suppliers by product type, considering only supplies that were active between '2017-01-01' and '2018-12-31' and for products that have been ordered by at least ten distinct customers?

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I mean the total purchase value across all suppliers combined, grouped by product type (i.e., one row per product type showing the sum of all purchase values from every supplier).
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH products_with_min_customers AS (
    SELECT oi.product_id
    FROM Order_Items oi
    JOIN Customer_Orders co ON oi.order_id = co.order_id
    GROUP BY oi.product_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT co.customer_id) >= 10
),
active_supplies AS (
    SELECT ps.product_id, ps.total_value_purchased
    FROM Product_Suppliers ps
    WHERE ps.date_supplied_from <= '2018-12-31'
      AND (ps.date_supplied_to IS NULL OR ps.date_supplied_to >= '2017-01-01')
)
SELECT p.product_type_code AS product_type,
       SUM(a.total_value_purchased) AS total_purchase_value
FROM active_supplies a
JOIN products_with_min_customers pmc ON a.product_id = pmc.product_id
JOIN Products p ON a.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_type_code;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I want the total purchase value for each supplier separately, still grouped by product type (i.e., a row for each supplier‑product‑type combination).
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH product_customer_counts AS (
    SELECT oi.product_id
    FROM Order_Items oi
    JOIN Customer_Orders co ON oi.order_id = co.order_id
    GROUP BY oi.product_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT co.customer_id) >= 10
)
SELECT s.supplier_name,
       p.product_type_code,
       SUM(ps.total_value_purchased) AS total_purchase_value
FROM Product_Suppliers ps
JOIN Suppliers s ON ps.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
JOIN Products p ON ps.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE ps.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM product_customer_counts)
  AND ps.date_supplied_from >= '2017-01-01'
  AND ps.date_supplied_from <= '2018-12-31'
GROUP BY s.supplier_name, p.product_type_code
ORDER BY s.supplier_name, p.product_type_code;

questions.nlq: Could you tell me which products were ordered across all department stores in 2018?

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I mean the products that appear in orders from every single department store - the ones they all have in common.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT p.product_name
FROM Products p
JOIN Order_Items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN Customer_Orders co ON oi.order_id = co.order_id
WHERE strftime('%Y', co.order_date) = '2018'
GROUP BY p.product_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ds.dept_store_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Department_Stores)
ORDER BY p.product_name

questions.nlq: Could you tell me the cumulative total value purchased of products supplied by all suppliers over time?

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I mean the cumulative total value purchased over time of the products that every supplier supplies (i.e., the products common to all suppliers).
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH total_suppliers AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM Suppliers
),
common_products AS (
    SELECT product_id
    FROM Product_Suppliers
    GROUP BY product_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT supplier_id) = (SELECT cnt FROM total_suppliers)
)
SELECT
    date_supplied_from,
    SUM(total_value_purchased) OVER (
        ORDER BY date_supplied_from
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS cumulative_total_value
FROM Product_Suppliers
WHERE product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM common_products)
ORDER BY date_supplied_from;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I mean, for each supplier, the cumulative total value purchased over time of the products that supplier supplies.
meanings.gt_sql: SELECT "supplier_id", SUM("total_value_purchased") AS "cumulative_total_value_purchased" FROM "Product_Suppliers" GROUP BY "supplier_id";
